turns.t: Oh doctor, thank you for seeing us so fast. Kabir came off his bike an hour ago and he's holding his wrist and crying.
Hello Kabir. I'm Dr Rahman. Can you show me where it hurts? ~
Here.
Okay. How did you fall? ~
The bike went over a bump, and I put my hand out. ~
He landed on his outstretched hand, doctor. On the road, not the grass. ~
Did you hit your head, Mum?
No, he had his helmet on, thank God. He didn't hit his head, no.
What's his age, and does he have any medicines?
He's nine. I gave him a spoon of paracetamol, 250 mg, when we got home, in case.
Good thinking. Any broken bones in the family?
His grandfather broke his wrist, years ago, but that's all.
Kabir, I'm going to touch your arm very gently, and I want you to tell me when it hurts.
Ow! Here! ~
Thank you, you're very brave. Mum, the wrist is swollen and tender over the end of the forearm bone, and he doesn't want to turn his hand over. ~
Is it broken? ~
I can't rule out a fracture, which is common at this age, so I'd like an X-ray of the wrist and forearm now.
Now? Right. ~
The nurse will take you through. In the meantime, keep the arm still in this sling, and give him nothing to eat or drink in case he needs a procedure.
Okay. Kabir, be brave. ~
Will I need a cast? ~
If it's broken, maybe. A lot of children's breaks are small and heal quickly. ~
Can I choose the colour? ~
Absolutely. ~
Thank you, doctor. ~
I'll come and see you with the picture in a few minutes. If his fingers go blue, cold or numb in the meantime, call us at once.
I will. ~
Mummy, don't leave. ~
I'm here, beta. ~
Good boy. See you shortly. ~
